title: Electron Ptychography via Differentiable Programming
content: Electron ptychography has long served as a prominent technique for addressing “missing phase” problems in materials characterization [1, 2]. When a high-energy electron wave traverses a sample, it acquires both phase shifts and intensity modulations, each encoding critical structural information about the specimen’s electrostatic potential [3]. Because traditional electron detectors capture only intensities, the phase component is effectively lost, motivating the need for specialized reconstruction methods. Ptychography recovers this hidden phase by collecting a series of spatially overlapping diffraction patterns while scanning a finely focused electron probe across the sample. The redundancy introduced by this scanning procedure provides sufficient constraints to retrieve phase information [4].
